1.title: CSS Specificity
1.concept: Specificity is the system browsers use to determine which CSS property values are most relevant to an element and should be applied. Inline styles carry the highest weight, followed by IDs, then classes/attributes, and finally element selectors.

2.title: The Box Model
2.task: Visualize margin vs padding on a div
2.concept: Every HTML element is rendered as a rectangular box. The CSS Box Model consists of the actual content area, padding (space inside the border), the border itself, and margin (space outside the border). Using box-sizing: border-box simplifies layout math.

3.title: Custom Properties
3.task: Create 3 CSS variables for a color scheme
3.concept: CSS variables (custom properties) allow you to store values globally in a stylesheet and reuse them throughout your layout. Declaring variables inside the :root pseudo-class makes them accessible globally.

4.title: Pseudo-classes
4.concept: Pseudo-classes are keywords added to selectors that specify a special state of the targeted elements. They allow you to style elements based on user interaction or structural position without altering the HTML.

5.title: Pseudo-elements
5.concept: Pseudo-elements are keywords appended to selectors that let you style a specific part of an element. The ::before and ::after pseudo-elements can inject cosmetic content visually using the 'content' property.

6.title: Transitions
6.concept: CSS transitions provide a way to control animation speed when changing CSS properties. Instead of property changes taking effect immediately, you can make them happen over a duration of time.

7.title: Transforms
7.task: Scale & rotate a card on hover
7.concept: The transform property applies 2D or 3D modifications to an element. It lets you translate (move), rotate, scale, and skew elements without disrupting the normal document flow or shifting surrounding items.

8.title: Flexbox Basics
8.concept: Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout model designed for laying out items in rows or columns. Activating 'display: flex' on a container turns it into a flex container, giving you powerful alignment properties along its main and cross axes.

9.title: Flex Direction
9.task: Build a row nav that wraps on small screens
9.concept: The flex-direction property configures the direction of the main axis (row or column). Pairing this with flex-wrap: wrap ensures that flex children automatically wrap to the next line if screen width runs out.

10.title: CSS Grid Intro
10.concept: CSS Grid is a two-dimensional grid-based layout framework. It allows you to align content into rows and columns. The fractional unit (fr) divides container space proportionally.

11.title: Grid Areas
11.concept: Grid areas let you assign semantic names to blocks of space on your page and sketch your layout directly within your CSS using the grid-template-areas property.

12.title: Responsive Units
12.task: Use rem, vw, clamp() in one layout
12.concept: Responsive typography avoids fixed pixel sizes. 'rem' scales text relative to the root browser font size, while 'clamp()' establishes mathematical floor, fluid, and ceiling values for text sizing.

13.title: Media Queries
13.task: Collapse a 2-col layout to 1 on mobile
13.concept: Media queries use conditional blocks based on properties like screen resolution or width. They allow you to apply tailored styling rules to handle different device screens elegantly.

14.title: CSS Animations
14.concept: CSS animations let you transition elements through multiple states smoothly. The @keyframes rule specifies the CSS styles the element will have at explicit timeline markers.

15.title: let vs const
15.concept: 'const' creates a block-scoped block configuration identifier whose value cannot be reassigned. Use 'let' when values must shift, such as tracking counters or conditional states.

16.title: Arrow Functions
16.concept: Arrow functions provide a shorter syntax for writing function expressions. They lack their own binding context for 'this', 'arguments', 'super', or 'new.target'.

17.title: Template Literals
17.task: Build a greeting string with variables
17.concept: Template literals are string literals wrapped in backticks (``). They allow for embedded JavaScript expressions via string interpolation structures and handle multi-line strings easily.

18.title: Destructuring
18.task: Destructure an object and an array
18.concept: Destructuring assignment syntax is a JavaScript expression that makes it possible to unpack values from arrays, or properties from objects, directly into distinct, clean variables.

19.title: Spread & Rest
19.concept: The spread operator (...) expands arrays or objects into individual elements. The rest syntax uses the exact same token to bundle multiple distinct function parameters down into a unified array.

20.title: Array Methods
20.concept: '.filter()' runs a test callback against each array item and builds a subset containing only items that match. '.map()' loops through each element to generate an entirely new, altered array.
20.code: const baseNumbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];\nconst oddNumbers = baseNumbers.filter(n => n % 2 !== 0); // [1, 3, 5]\nconst formatted = baseNumbers.map(n => `Item #${n}`);

21.title: Promises Basics
21.task: Write a fetch() and log the result
21.concept: A Promise represents the eventual completion or failure of an asynchronous operation and its resulting value. It acts as a proxy for a value not necessarily known when the promise is created.

22.title: DOM Selection
22.concept: The Document Object Model treats HTML documents as a structural tree of nodes. querySelector stands as the industry standard, fetching target node elements using standard CSS selector strings.

23.title: DOM Manipulation
23.task: Add/remove a class on button click
23.concept: JavaScript updates layouts safely by editing active node attributes. Modifying strings via the classList API isolates look-and-feel logic inside your CSS sheets.

24.title: Event Listeners
24.task: Toggle dark mode with a button
24.concept: Event listeners listen for user interactions like clicks, scrolling, or key presses. addEventListener connects an element node to a callback task execution structure.

25.title: Forms & Input
25.task: Read an input value and display it live
25.concept: User entries inside standard form fields are stored within the node's live '.value' parameter. Catch adjustments in real time by listening directly to the 'input' event lifecycle.

26.title: Local Storage
26.task: Save a user name between page refreshes
26.concept: Local Storage allows web applications to store string keys and values locally within the user's browser without expiration data limits. Complex structures must be serialized via JSON utilities.

27.title: Fetch API
27.task: Load JSON from a free public API
27.concept: The Fetch API gives JavaScript full utility powers to perform network HTTP queries. Wrapping operations inside async/await blocks cleans up code structure asynchronously.

28.title: Mini Project: To-Do
28.task: Build a to-do list from scratch
28.concept: Combine input reading, manual element generation with 'document.createElement', and list node insertion via '.appendChild()' to dynamically update application markup structures.

29.title: Mini Project: Advanced To-Do
29.task: Add delete + done to your to-do list
29.concept: Event handling allows you to configure interactive element triggers during creation. Use parent targeting or targeted removal APIs like '.remove()' to clear nodes dynamically.

30.title: Review Day
30.task: Revisit your hardest day and redo its task
30.concept: Deliberate repetition forms robust memory connections. Rebuilding demanding code layouts from a blank page reveals optimization paths and strengthens core troubleshooting skills.
